text:
Marcos: Quick share — ran a warmup vs steady-state microbench across quant modes on long context (32k). Surprising hotspot: prefill write path for INT8/4-bit dominates TTFT even though decode per-token is cheaper.

Ali: Can you paste the numbers?

Marcos: Bench summary (model-x / seq=32k / single GPU):
```
config: batch sizes 1/4/16, microbatcher=static(16)
Prefill end-to-end latency (ms): FP16: 1200 / 400 / 80
INT8: 1450 / 470 / 95
FP8: 1320 / 430 / 88
4bit: 1600 / 520 / 110

Decode per-token (µs): FP16: 200 | INT8: 240 | FP8: 220 | 4bit: 280
TTFT @ batch=1: FP16 1200ms, INT8 1450ms, FP8 1320ms
TPS steady-state @ batch=16: FP16 1250 tok/s, INT8 1380 tok/s, FP8 1310 tok/s
```

Priya: So decode TPS for INT8 is higher but prefill TTFT is worse — matches hypothesis that KV write+layout conversion is the bottleneck. :thinking:

Marcos: Exactly. Hotspots from perf trace:
```
hot functions (wall):
  kv_write_dequantize_kernel   36%
  memcpy_async                  22%
  nv_transform_quant_to_kv      18%
  attention_forward             12%
  other                         12%
``` 
The dequant+memcpy is during prefill (writing KV), decode mostly hits quantized fast-path.

Jin: What kernels selected for KV? Are we forcing fallback to float32 layout for write?

Marcos: Kernel selector chooses "quantized-kv-write + dequantize-on-write" for compatibility. We have a fallback codepath that converts to float16 layout on write for some models — that's the expensive part.

Perf-bot: perf-bot: Regression alert — prefill latency INT8 +18% vs last tagged baseline (2026-03-10).

Ali: Did you try writing KV in packed quant format and dequantizing lazily on eviction/read? Lazy dequant could shift cost to first decode hit but lower TTFT.

Marcos: I ran a quick sim: lazy-deq reduced prefill TTFT by ~30% for INT8, but first decode on a cold KV entry paid +40% per-token for that token only. For our latency SLOs that trade looks good for low fanout requests.

Priya: Also curious about microbatching: static microbatch=16 increases KV write contention. Adaptive microbatching based on available GPU memory and pending prefill queue might reduce peak memcpys.

Jin: Actionable experiments:
- implement lazy-dequantize-on-read with option toggle
- add an adaptive microbatcher that reduces prefill batch size when KV backlog > X
- run long-context 64k sweep for FP8/INT8/4bit with both strategies

Marcos: I'll sketch the lazy-deq PR and perf harness. I have a prototype microbatch tweak; will push perf numbers by EOD.

Ali: If lazy-deq lands, we should add per-route policy: prefer TTFT (low-latency) vs prefer TPS (throughput) so users can pick deq-on-write vs lazy-deq.

Perf-bot: perf-bot: Note — add regression test target: prefill_int8_ttft <= baseline * 1.05 when policy=deq-on-write.

Priya: Nice. Also add telemetry: bytes moved during prefill, count of dequant ops on write vs read.

Jin: I'll own microbatcher, Marcos you own lazy-deq. Create tickets and tag eng-runtime. 

Marcos: created draft PR link: https://repo.internal/r/redwood/rt/compare/warmup-lazy-deq

Ali: Thanks — validate with perf harness and let's sync Thursday.

Marcos: ack :tada:
